interpretations.text: Albrecht Dürer's Knight, Death, and the Devil presents a Christian knight riding forward while Death holds an hourglass and a swine-snouted devil trails behind. The knight does not flee; he proceeds with disciplined calm. Often read as an allegory of the steadfast soul moving through a world of temptation and mortality—courage as continuity of purpose rather than absence of fear. Time (the hourglass) is acknowledged, not denied.
Austere, resolute, slightly grim. The landscape is harsh; companionship is sparse (the dog). Fits themes of perseverance, moral focus, walking one's path despite reminders of death.
Detailed engraving, armored rider on horseback in profile, rocky path, castle on distant ridge, dense linework, high contrast black and white.
